planDocument: dispatch://INFRA-625/artifact/plan-md (the same text is the plan below; spike patches, harnesses and raw tables are committed under .legion/INFRA-625/spikes/)
summary: Four dependency patches (micromark 4.0.2 lazy-line scan, micromark-core-commonmark 2.0.3 label-end, micromark-extension-gfm-footnote 2.1.0 call scan, mdast-util-from-markdown 2.0.3 prepareList) make every named shape linear; a legion-owned list/quote nesting bound equal to Go's maxNesting (100) with a blank-line fast path ends the stack overflows and quadratic chains; bodies over 4,000 characters are parsed in a module Web Worker on every read-only surface so none holds the main thread for a second; Go mints block ids in batches and skips tab expansion in tab-free sources; resolveContentExits splits into five rule functions plus placeExits.

implement: legion-worker: the phase rules, the proof object and its negative control (references/pr-body.md), tools.md for the browser harness, conflicts-and-rewrites.md if main must come in
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass on the settled diff before the proof at the head that merges
dispatch: the plan.md artifact and any message to a person on the issue
test: legion-worker: re-running the implementer's proof on the tester's own lane, the proof object and negative control (references/pr-body.md), and the issue-pod browser harness (references/tools.md)
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md for approval and references/review-threads.md for threads; the reviewer checks the fuzz counts, the bound's parity with pmdoc's maxNesting and the repository rules the plan lists
ce-simplify-code: judging whether the implementer's simplify pass left reuse, quality or efficiency findings

findings.finding: A1's 'draws in under 1 s' has two readings (main-thread gap vs time to the formatted list), and no design makes the plain 8,000-item list parse under 1 s; the worker leaves 579-1,381 ms of main-thread drawing for it.
findings.answer: Decision 1: A1 is proven as INFRA-581 proved the identical words, a heartbeat gap under 1,000 ms reset at the first comments request, with the time to the formatted body recorded as an annotation; departure recorded for the architect. The drawing cost is cut with content-visibility on long bodies' items, with a measured fallback rule (sliced appends) if the in-app gap stays above 600 ms.

findings.finding: The worker is a third mechanism the spec does not offer and breaks 14 sync-dependent sites.
findings.answer: Decision 2 and D3: in scope, recorded as a departure; the plan carries its contract (data-markdown-pending distinct from data-markdown-fallback, previous paint kept on updates, newest answer wins, portals recomputed per paint, reader's place kept across a late paint) and acceptance A5 with rows and unit tests.

findings.finding: 'All three' engines: the editor/default mode is neither fixed nor measured.
findings.answer: Decision 3: the patches and the bound reach every engine (shared micromark constructs); proof-editor tests lock the default mode's timing per shape; the editor keeps the plain list's linear ~1.4 s in a version view or paste, recorded as a departure.

findings.finding: The document cap is 1 MiB and 65,536 elements, not the 32,000-character body cap.
findings.answer: The bound targets the body cap; the document-write row asserts each 32,000-character body's verdict (stored or refused 400) under 1 s; longer documents get the linear fixes but no absolute bound (stated in 'does not change').

findings.finding: Go's nesting bound does not back comments, so a comment past 100 blocks reading as text is an owner's decision.
findings.answer: Decision 4: mirrors the architect's INFRA-581 decision for ':::'; today such a comment overflows the stack from ~650 '- '. Named in the completion summary for the architect.

findings.finding: The blank-line fast path and the prepareList patch touch list spread, which sjawhar/legion#2481 is also changing.
findings.answer: Both are proven output-identical by the fuzz (0 differences, spread included); whichever of the two merges second regenerates fixtures and re-runs bun run check, differential.sh and the fuzz (repository rules section).

findings.finding: No machine check for 'reads as it would otherwise' although the repo has a documented fuzz bar.
findings.answer: Task 8 and A4: at least 60,000 generated documents over the learning's full alphabet plus CommonMark examples and the pmdoc corpus, oracle the unpatched packages, 0 differences for D1 and the fast path, only Go-refused documents for D2, kept differences become corpus fixtures.

findings.finding: The worker's decoder alias is global; the realm-wide construct wrap reaches the fixture generator and could miss a duplicate micromark-core-commonmark copy.
findings.answer: Decision 6: one decoder (index.js) in page and worker, with a differential across Chromium, WebKit and Firefox; D2: the wrap is idempotent, runs from lib-remark-directive-plugin.ts in every bundle and the generator, and a test through a bare remark-parse processor fails on a duplicate copy.

findings.finding: A Go wall-clock 1 s bound contradicts pmdoc's CPU-time convention and its -race job.
findings.answer: The Go test asserts CPU time under 1 s in non-race builds (build-tagged constant) and growsLinearly in both; the API wall time is the e2e document-write row; the goldmark fork is dropped (decision 5).

findings.finding: Surfaces the spec names are missed: messages, asks, hover cards (MarkdownPreview parses the full source), the Inbox, the live view.
findings.answer: The worker sits in markdown-engine's single entry used by every surface; e2e rows for the plain list as a message, an ask question and a hover card; the live view's streaming is covered by the previous-paint rule and unit tests.

findings.finding: content-visibility is unmeasured in the app and meets the one-measurement scroll contract.
findings.answer: Applied only to bodies painted from the worker path (class dispatch-markdown-long); measured in the app with a stated fallback rule; the reader's-place rows run in Chromium and WebKit; rows assert li counts, not visibility.

findings.finding: New e2e rows could pass on a pending literal paint; WebKit coverage unstated.
findings.answer: Every row asserts the formatted body (li counts, nesting depth) and zero data-markdown-pending and data-markdown-fallback; the spec joins the webkit and firefox projects' testMatch.

findings.finding: Unsourced claims: architect acceptance of the heartbeat, the 24-block rejection, the 4,000 threshold basis, the 21.7 s vs 33-36 s generators, worker size/boot, the fork approval rule, the production check.
findings.answer: Heartbeat acceptance cited to INFRA-581's acceptance at fc1e2366 and stated as a departure; the 24-block bound rejected because it changes Go-accepted readings; the threshold derived from post-fix worst density and proven by a 3,999-character row; each e2e row names its exact body; size and boot from the worker spike's table; the fork rule cited to the deployment instructions' approval-first list; the production check reads the build and page only, nothing posted.

findings.finding: The resolveContentExits split has no acceptance and an ambiguous function count.
findings.answer: Decision 9: five rule functions (one per doc-comment bullet) plus placeExits, resolveContentExits as driver; A6: every proof-editor test, bun run check and the fuzz unchanged.

specDepartures.spec: Change 2: each list body no larger than the body cap parses in well under a second in all three engines; A1: a comment holding each list shape draws on the Conversation tab in under 1 s.
specDepartures.plan: Every superlinear shape (lazy lines, bracket runs, deep chains) parses well under a second in every engine. The plain 8,000-item list and 100 nested items with blank lines stay linear at about 1.4-1.5 s in Chromium; for them A1 is met as INFRA-581 met it, a main-thread heartbeat gap under 1,000 ms, by parsing in a worker; the formatted body arrives after the worker answers and the text shows at once.
specDepartures.evidence: Spikes on this branch: read-only parse after all four patches and the bound, list_plain 1,390-1,455 ms, nest100_blanks 1,471 ms (Chromium); worker path main-thread gap list_plain 579 ms idle, nest100_blanks 104 ms.

acceptance: A1's 'draws in under 1 s' is proven as the longest main-thread gap under 1,000 ms, with time to the formatted body recorded, not asserted, for the plain and nested-with-blank-lines lists

specDepartures.spec: Change 2: by a parse fix, or by a bound that keeps the reader's text as it would read otherwise; the implementer chooses.
specDepartures.plan: Both, plus a third mechanism: a module Web Worker parsing bodies over 4,000 characters for every read-only surface, with its own contract (pending marker, previous paint kept, newest answer wins, reader's place kept) and acceptance A5.
specDepartures.evidence: No parse fix brings the plain list under 1 s on the main thread (findings section 5); worker spike: engine runs in a worker after one bundler alias, output identical to the main-thread parse on 8 shapes.

outcome.scope: Adds off-main-thread parsing of long bodies in packages/dispatch/web (markdown-engine, useRenderedMarkdown, a new worker), a data-markdown-pending state, scroll compensation for late paints, and a page-bundle decoder change (+11.6 KB gz).

specDepartures.spec: Change 2: 'in all three' (read-only engine, default/editor engine, Go).
specDepartures.plan: The editor's default mode gets the patches and the nesting bound but no worker: a version view or paste of an 8,000-item list still parses on the page's thread in about 1.4 s. Opening a document is unaffected (loaded from its stored tree).
specDepartures.evidence: The worker serves the read-only engine only (markdown-engine.ts:134-137); the live editor parses markdown only in setMarkdown and paste.

outcome.scope: The editor's version view and paste keep the plain list's linear cost; the superlinear shapes and the bound are fixed there.

decisionsForTheArchitect: A comment nested past 100 blocks (Go's count) reads as text past that point, as INFRA-581 decided for ':::' past 32.
The goldmark fork is dropped: creating a fork repository is approval-first under the deployment instructions, and normal-build Go already meets 1 s.
